title: Restriction to a localized site commutes with the sheaf tensor product
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$. Let $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ be the localized ringed site and $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F|_U$ restriction of sheaves of modules to it [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf tensor products as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules
$$
(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)|_U\cong\mathcal F|_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal G|_U,
$$
natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$, which for every object $V\to U$ of $\mathcal C/U$ and all $x\in\mathcal F(V)$, $y\in\mathcal G(V)$ sends the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on $\mathcal C$ to the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on $\mathcal C/U$. No finiteness or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, applied to the localization morphism $(j_U,j_U^\sharp)$ of Tag 03DH (section-localize, definition-localize-ringed-site), for which $j_U^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F|_U$.

proof.text: Put $P=\mathcal F\otimes_{p,\mathcal O}\mathcal G$ and $Q=\mathcal F|_U\otimes_{p,\mathcal O_U}\mathcal G|_U$. At $(V\to U)$ both $P|_U$ and $Q$ have value $\mathcal F(V)\otimes_{\mathcal O(V)}\mathcal G(V)$. Their restriction maps are the same maps induced by the restrictions of the two factors and of the coefficients. Thus $P|_U=Q$ as presheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules, naturally in both factors. The sheaf tensors in the assertion are $P^\#$ and $Q^\#$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 03DH, section-localize. Slice sheafification comparison is supplied by lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification.

proof.text: Apply the abelian-group case of the slice sheafification comparison to the underlying abelian presheaf of $P$. Module sheafification has this abelian sheafification as its underlying abelian sheaf. We obtain an abelian-sheaf isomorphism $c:Q^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}(P^\#)|_U$, natural in maps of $P$, with $c\eta_Q=(\eta_P)|_U$ on $Q=P|_U$. Here $\eta_P$ and $\eta_Q$ are the module sheafification units. Take a universe containing the site and all values, as in the cited slice result; no fibre products or subcanonicity of the site are required.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 03DH, section-localize. Slice sheafification comparison is supplied by lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification.

proof.text: The comparison $c$ is $\mathcal O_U$-linear: transport the module action on $(P^\#)|_U$ to $Q^\#$ through the abelian isomorphism $c$. The equation $c\eta_Q=(\eta_P)|_U$ shows that this transported action extends the action on $Q$, because the restricted unit is linear. The uniqueness of the extending module action in module sheafification identifies it with the given action on $Q^\#$. Hence $c$, and therefore $e=c^{-1}$, are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_U$-modules.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 03DH, section-localize. Slice sheafification comparison is supplied by lem-cbc-sieve-slice-sheafification.

proof.text: Take $e:(P^\#)|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}Q^\#$ for the requested isomorphism. For $x\in\mathcal F(V)$ and $y\in\mathcal G(V)$, the unit equation gives $e((\eta_P)_V(x\otimes y))=(\eta_Q)_{V/U}(x\otimes y)$, exactly the asserted formula. For maps $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F\prime$ and $g:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\prime$, the induced presheaf map sends $x\otimes y$ to $f(x)\otimes g(y)$, and the sectionwise identification in step 1 respects this map. Naturality of $c$ in that presheaf map, followed by inversion, is precisely naturality of $e$ in the two factors. No step uses flatness or finiteness.
